channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Russia Strikes Ukraine Overnight As Zelenskyy Denies Plans For Elections On War Anniversary
item.description: Russian forces launched overnight ballistic missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed reports that elections or a referendum on territorial integrity would be announced on the fourth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion.

item.title: Guns Or Cucumbers: The Kremlin's Wartime Economy Steers Into Serious Crosscurrents
item.description: On the verge of its fifth year of the Ukraine war, the Kremlin is fighting another stubborn enemy at home: high consumer prices and rising unhappiness among average Russians. The government wants to bring the economy back to earth; the question is whether it will be a hard or soft landing.

item.title: Ukrainian Skeleton Athlete Disqualified From Olympics Over Helmet Dispute
item.description: Vladyslav Heraskevych, a Ukrainian skeleton pilot, will not be allowed to compete in the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympic Winter Games after refusing to comply with guidelines of the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

item.title: Ukrainian Olympian Disqualified Over Helmet Honoring Athletes Killed In War
item.description: Ukrainian skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych was disqualified at the 2026 Winter Olympics after refusing to remove a helmet honoring athletes killed in Russia's war on Ukraine, which features portraits of more than 20 Ukrainian athletes killed since Russia’s full-scale invasion.

item.title: Max Cometh: What The Blocking Of WhatsApp, Telegram Means For Millions Of Russians
item.description: WhatsApp has long been the most popular messaging app for Russians, followed closely by Telegram. This week, officials took major steps to cut them off and make them unusable—part of a long-running, two-pronged effort to control the information Russians access online.

item.title: Massive Russian Drone Strikes Hit Dnipro, Odesa
item.description: Russia fired a massive wave of drones at Ukrainian cities in the early morning of February 12 as part of a nationwide attack on energy facilities that killed at least two people in eastern Ukraine.

item.title: Iranian State Media Reporter Says 'Death To Khamenei' On Air
item.description: An Iranian state television reporter said “Death to Khamenei” in a live broadcast at a government rally on February 11. The reporter later apologized in a social media post and said the remark was a verbal slip. The channel's broadcast director was reportedly dismissed in response to the slip-up.

item.title: Iranian Athletes, Actors Quietly Honor People Killed In Protest Crackdown
item.description: A trophy-winning women's soccer team in Iran, along with celebrated actors, joined in nationwide acts of solidarity with the thousands who were killed by state security forces in a crackdown in January on protests. Soccer players refused to show emotion, while actors boycotted awards.

item.title: New US Sanctions Bill Aims To Choke Off Kremlin Oil Revenue
item.description: US lawmakers have unveiled a bipartisan bill to tighten sanctions on Russia’s oil trade, targeting foreign buyers and “shadow fleet” loopholes to curb Kremlin revenue and increase leverage in any Ukraine war talks.

item.title: Rubio Says World At 'Defining Moment,' Jets Into Munich
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the world is at a “defining moment” as he headed for the Munich Security Conference (MSC), where he was expected to land early on February 13.
